name: gui
description: Run Linux GUI apps on the server and view/control them in the browser through xpra — adaptive, low-latency HTML5 remote display (much faster than X11 forwarding or VNC). Requires xpra installed on the host; see this extension's README.

gui.display.description: X11 display number xpra creates (e.g. ":100"). Only change this if it conflicts with another display already in use on the host.

gui.port.description: Preferred TCP port for xpra's HTML5/WebSocket server. If already in use, the next free port is picked automatically.

gui.quality.description: Encoding quality/latency tradeoff passed to xpra. Automatic adapts to network conditions on its own.

gui.dpi.description: DPI reported to X11 apps running on the display.

gui.mode.description: Individual apps: each launched app is its own window, composited by xpra directly. Full desktop: streams one whole desktop environment (its own window manager, taskbar, wallpaper) — needed for xfce4 or similar; don't launch a full desktop environment in Individual apps mode, its window manager will fight xpra's own. Takes effect on the next Start (stop first to switch an already-running session).

gui.desktopCommand.description: Full desktop mode only: the command that starts the desktop environment (e.g. xfce4-session, startlxde, mate-session). Must be installed on the host.

gui.resizeDisplay.description: Follow browser window: the remote display resizes to fill your browser tab/window, including when using xpra's own Fullscreen toggle — but xpra recalculates DPI on every resize, which can make the cursor and UI elements balloon in size at some window sizes. Fixed size: the display stays at its initial resolution and DPI never changes (the image scales to fit your window instead of resizing natively) — use this if you hit the oversized-cursor issue. Takes effect on the next Start.
